title: Removing the last entry takes the empty line after it, which would otherwise join the keep scalar before it
notes: The value of `x` is two line feeds after `two` (the empty line before `y`). If the empty line after `y: 1` stayed, it would follow the keep scalar directly and the value of `x` would gain a third line feed. Removing `y` must leave the value of `x` as it was, so that line goes with the entry. The comment line at the margin after the last entry stays.

provenance.reference: Found by comparing random edits of random documents with a plain model while building a lossless document for a Python library.
